decisions.question: What should count as good enough for the first classroom pilot?
decisions.why: This controls when Codex stops polishing and helps prepare a real teacher/iPad test.
options: A few successful real iPad scans with one worksheet and visible review flags
A full small-class dry run with saved results and teacher review
Defer to Codex recommendation after the next verification pass
decisions.recommendation: Aim for a full small-class dry run, but use a few successful real iPad scans as the next milestone.
decisions.answer: Defer to Codex recommendation after the next verification pass

decisions.question: What should the first TPT worksheet pack sound like?
decisions.why: The naming/copy direction should come from Tony's teacher and marketplace instincts.
decisions.recommendation: Start plain and teacher-convenience focused; avoid over-explaining ScanGrade until the app loop is proven.

decisions.question: When Codex has idle time, what class of work should it prefer?
decisions.why: This keeps paid Codex time useful without letting automation drift into risky production changes.
decisions.recommendation: Prefer verification and summaries first, then backlog/doc organization, then tiny test-only fixes when evidence is clear.

decisions.question: What makes a ScanGrade worksheet feel high quality enough for Tony to use, sell, and put the brand on?
decisions.why: Worksheet quality is a major unresolved product area: white space, density, fonts, illustrations, color, fun vs academic tone, and what makes Tony reject a TPT worksheet.
options: Let Codex draft 3 visual directions first
Defer until after student handwriting tests
decisions.recommendation: Schedule a dedicated worksheet-design interview after the first real sample test, then let Codex turn it into templates.

decisions.question: How should Mission Control batch questions so Codex can keep working without interrupting Tony constantly?
decisions.why: Tony wants one place for accumulated decisions, options, recommendations, and deferrable questions rather than scattered interruptions.
options: Let Codex decide when to surface questions
decisions.recommendation: Use priority-only interruptions plus a visible backlog queue; include a 'defer to Codex recommendation' option when safe.
decisions.answer: Use priority-only interruptions plus a visible backlog queue. Batch and rank questions as Must answer soon, Can defer, or Codex recommends default; keep working on safe adjacent tasks.

decisions.question: Can Codex make tiny UI polish improvements while Tony is away?
decisions.why: Small visual improvements can make ScanGrade feel cleaner and more trustworthy without waiting for a full redesign conversation.
options: Ask Tony before any visual change
decisions.recommendation: Allow minimal reversible UI polish when it improves clarity, spacing, hierarchy, contrast, mobile fit, or visual calm, but require Tony approval for major redesigns, new workflows, or brand shifts.
decisions.answer: Allow minimal reversible UI polish consistent with the clean ScanGrade teacher-trust aesthetic.

decisions.question: Can Codex prepare TPT and marketing artifacts before the classroom sample test is finished?
decisions.why: Tony wants Codex to keep using available time productively, but the marketplace promise must not get ahead of actual classroom evidence.
options: Prepare publish-ready assets after Tony review
Pause TPT work until student samples are tested
decisions.recommendation: Prepare internal drafts, product frameworks, preview concepts, and conservative copy now; wait for Tony approval and classroom evidence before publishing or making scan/automation claims.
decisions.answer: Prepare internal drafts and frameworks now. Publishing, final claims, and customer-facing promises wait for Tony and real sample evidence.

decisions.question: What should ScanGrade do at different confidence levels: auto-grade, flag for review, or refuse to grade?
decisions.why: Trust thresholds are central to teacher trust, student feedback, practice mode, assessment mode, and whether review saves time.
options: Assessment-safe: refuse or require teacher review when uncertain
decisions.recommendation: Use different thresholds by mode: more forgiving in practice, conservative in assessment, and always review/refuse when the app cannot explain itself.
